en.html:
The refugees—people who had come into Kamakura asking for shelter from the war—mostly lived in parks or on vacant land kept as firebreaks. Good living conditions, these were not.

Here, a shack counted as a superior residence. Most people had tents, or arrangements which one had to be generous enough to call tents. Looking at this, I could understand how rumors that they had spread disease had taken hold.

...Now. How to begin?

Following the two men, I had crossed the downstream bridge. Far and inconvenient, they had said. On both points I could now give my personal confirmation. I had reached the settlement, but catching hold of the nearest person and asking a few casual questions was plainly not going to work here.

People were probably there. Showing themselves, no. I could sense them keeping very quiet and watching us.

We appeared to be under a most thorough examination. Given the bad relations and clashes with the established residents, their suspicion was understandable. But with them studying us and us studying them, the investigation would consist entirely of staring.

Should I call out? In this atmosphere I might only make them more suspicious. Still—

ja.html:
難民――つまり戦災からの庇護を求めて鎌倉へ流入
した人々の多くは、火除地とされていた空地や公園に
住居を構えている。
　当然だが、その環境は良いものではない。

　<ruby>掘っ立て小屋<rt>バラック</rt></ruby>ならむしろ上等。大半はテントないし
テントとも呼べないような代物だった。
　病気を流行らせたという噂が立つのも、仕方のない
面はある。

　……さて、どうしたものか。

　二人の男を追うようにして下流の橋――確かに遠く
不便だった――を渡り、難民居住地へ来てはみたが。
　そこらの人を適当に捕まえて話を聞く、という空気
ではない。

　人はいるのだろうが、姿を見せてくれなかった。
　息を潜めてこちらを窺う気配である。

　どうも酷く警戒されているようだ。
　旧来住民との間柄が良くなく、衝突も発生している
現状では無理からぬ態度だが……といって、このまま
見合っていても埒は明かない。

　こちらから呼び掛けてみるか？
　この空気ではかえって警戒を深めさせる結果になり
かねないが、しかし――

I stopped halfway and hesitated. In what capacity was I asking? That would have to be stated. But would identifying myself as police improve matters with this man?

A welcome with open arms was probably not coming. On the other hand, without mentioning the police, my official designation remained Yesterday's Drunkard. Under that designation I could hardly expect a serious hearing.

...Kya karein. The introduction would have to be made.

Yes. Precisely the welcome anticipated. The young man's face visibly tightened; all around us, the quiet presences began to stir.

By law, these people could not be counted as regular citizens of Kamakura. For them, the police were not protectors. Quite possibly the opposite. I quickly tried to remove that fear, before my introduction did any more work on its own.

en.html:
So these were people driven out by the struggle between Raichou Imagawa and Yukitsura Ashikaga in Kinki and Tokai. The fight for control of Rokuhara had been fierce. These people's homes had gone in it; they had escaped as far as Kamakura.

Go back, go somewhere else—probably neither option was left to them now.

He answered with a shrug. A question whose answer required no asking, and I had asked it.

The same troubles were spreading among the regular citizens. Here they existed in a more severe form. For solving that, my capabilities were not sufficient. We could only hope for the authorities to act in the future.

Something smaller, perhaps. That was the scale on which I could be of use.

Kageaki"I have also heard there is trouble between you and the established residents."
Refugee B"Haan... we are not welcome. So this trouble, that trouble, something keeps happening."
Refugee B"Honestly, their side I understand. A whole crowd in dirty clothes suddenly pours into your town. Who will feel happy about that?"
Kageaki"..."
Refugee B"But we came here because there was nowhere else. They say get out. Achha, get out and go where? We cannot just nod and leave."
Kageaki"Yes."
Refugee B"Somehow... I wish they would accept us."
Kageaki"I understand there was an incident that made relations much worse."
Refugee B"The bridge, you mean?"
Kageaki"Yes."
Refugee B"They say we broke it. We would never do that..."
Refugee B"Who here has that much energy left, you tell me?"
Kageaki"..."
Refugee B"And benefit? What benefit comes to us? Nothing. It is complete bakwaas."
Kageaki"Then who do you think did it?"
Refugee B"Who knows? Some troublemaker having his fun, maybe?"
Refugee B"Otherwise... I don't want to think like this, but... maybe the residents broke it themselves. To get an excuse for throwing us out—"
Kageaki"..."
Refugee B"...Haa. Now bakwaas is coming from my mouth also."
Refugee B"But impossible, I cannot call it. I understand why they suspect us... this feeling I am having, probably they are having the same one."
Kageaki"...Yes. Probably."
Refugee B"Kya haal hai..."

難民Ｂ「ああ……俺達は歓迎されてないからな。 　あれこれと揉め事は起きてるよ」
難民Ｂ「実を言えば、住民側あいつらの気持ちはわかる。 　自分の町にいきなり薄汚い格好した連中が 大勢なだれ込んできたら、誰だって嫌な気分 になるだろうさ」
景明「……」
難民Ｂ「けど俺達は他に行き場が無くてここに来た んだ。 　出ていけと言われても、そうですかと頷け やしない」
景明「ええ」
難民Ｂ「どうにか……受け入れて欲しいんだが」
景明「何やら、関係を決定的に悪化させる事件が あったとか」
難民Ｂ「橋のことだな？」
景明「はい」
難民Ｂ「あいつらは俺達が壊したって言ってる。 　でも、やるわけがない……」
難民Ｂ「ここの誰にそんな元気があるってんだ」
景明「……」
難民Ｂ「しかも何の得にもならないじゃないか。 　馬鹿げてるよ」
景明「では、貴方は何者の犯行だと思われます？」
難民Ｂ「さあなぁ。 　どこかの悪たれの悪戯じゃないのか？」
難民Ｂ「でなければ……考えたくはないが…… 　住民側が俺達を追い出す口実作りに自分で 壊した、なんてことも――」
景明「……」
難民Ｂ「……ふぅ。 　俺も馬鹿なこと言ってるな」
難民Ｂ「でも、有り得ないとは思えないんだ。 　向こうが俺達を疑うのもわかるよ……要は 今の俺と同じ気持ちなんだろう」
景明「……そうですね。おそらく」
難民Ｂ「やれやれ、だ」
